chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled regarding pre-emptive right (shuf'ah) among partners in lands and dwellings, and said, 'No harm and no causing harm.' And he said, 'When boundaries are marked and limits are set, there is no pre-emptive right.'

key_terms.الشُّفْعَةِ: Pre-emptive right; the right of a partner or co-owner to buy out another's share before it is sold to a third party.
key_terms.الْأُرُفُ: Boundaries or limits; the physical demarcations of a property.
key_terms.الْحُدُودُ: Limits or borders; the established boundaries of a property.
key_terms.بَيْنَ الشُّرَكَاءِ: Among partners; referring to co-owners of a property.
key_terms.لَا ضَرَرَ وَ لَا ضِرَارَ: No harm and no causing harm; a fundamental legal maxim in Islamic jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the right of pre-emption (shuf'ah) to be valid in Islamic law?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), grounding the pre-emptive right (*shuf'ah*) in the Prophetic maxim 'no harm and no harming,' which Shia jurists cite as a foundational principle for preventing injustice in shared ownership. The narration specifies that this right is contingent upon the property remaining undivided; once boundaries (*hudud*) are clearly established, the potential for harm from a new co-owner diminishes, thereby extinguishing the right of pre-emption.
